title: David Brent Champions Community Access Through The Hudson River Museum
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_markdown:
In Westchester County, New York, The Hudson River Museum brings New York locals together through engaging arts, science and history exhibits, while supporting the community through outreach and interdisciplinary programs. David Brent, Vice President, Global Head of Data Vantage Market Data and Solutions Sales, received Cboe’s 2025 Outstanding Community Service Award for his volunteer work with the museum and commitment to the New York community.


David was introduced to The Hudson River Museum at his previous job and has been volunteering there for three years. He initially started volunteering at the museum because it allowed him to build new connections in Westchester and stay up to date with community events. Plus, David enjoys how the museum brings people together to support local initiatives that benefit the broader community.


*David in front of the Glenview wing of the museum*


He now serves on the Board of Trustees of the museum and he initially got involved on the finance committee, leveraging his professional experience to support the museum’s financial initiatives. He later joined the development committee to focus on relationship building and fundraising. More recently, David has focused on connecting with people in the area to increase awareness of the museum.


The Hudson River Museum prioritizes community engagement by hosting events that are tied to cultural celebrations and offers programming for people of all ages. Entry to the museum is free on Fridays, removing financial barriers and underscoring the importance of access for everyone.


*Lunar New Year celebration at the museum*


“The museum creates an environment where everyone in the community feels welcome,” David says. “It helps break down the perception that museums are exclusive or elitist spaces.”


The benefits of museums go beyond something to do. David highlighted the tangible benefits of exposure to arts programs, including higher graduation rates, lower dropout rates and increased likelihood of community involvement later in life.


“Many former participants in the Hudson River Museum’s Junior Docent Program return as a donors,” he says. “It’s just one example of the long-term impact these programs have and how the cycle of giving back works,” David says.


Funding is crucial to the longevity of the museum, ensuring its ability to provide thought-provoking exhibits, arts and activities. The museum relies on federal funding as well as local and private funding to sustain operations. The museum’s annual gala also helps raise funds and brings New York locals together in celebration of art, science and history.


In honor of David’s contributions, Cboe donated $5,000 to the Hudson River Museum to support the important community-centered programming and accessibility to the arts in New York.[Learn more](https://www.hrm.org/) about The Hudson River Museum today.
